title: Skim Milk Flocculation and RNA Extraction for SARS-CoV-2 Viral Capture
author: Jillian Dunbar
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.b2uwqexe
materials: Aliquot 700 µL of Buffer RW1 Qiagen Catalog #1053394 to the RNeasy spin column. Centrifuge for 00:00:30 at full speed. Discard filtrate.
Aliquot 500 µL of Buffer RPE Qiagen Catalog #1018013 to the RNeasy spin column. Centrifuge for 00:00:30 at full speed. Discard filtrate.
Aliquot 800 µL of Buffer RLT Qiagen Catalog #79216 from the Qiagen RNeasy Mini Kit (Cat. No. 74106) into the centrifuge bottle.
If using a Lab Paddler Stomacher:
Autoclave Skim Milk Solution before using.

steps.title: Prepare Stock Solutions
steps.instruction: Prepare the necessary stock solutions for the elution and flocculation processes.

substeps.instruction: Prepare Tween 80 stock: dissolve 1 mL of Polyoxyethylene-80 (Bio Basic Inc. Catalog #TB0562.SIZE.500ml) in 100 mL distilled water.
Prepare Antifoam A stock: dissolve 1 mL of Antifoam A in 100 mL distilled water.
Prepare NaPP stock: dissolve 1 g of NaPP in 100 mL distilled water.
Prepare 10X PBS Solution: Mix 80 g NaCl, 2 g KCl, 14.4 g Na2HPO4, and 2.4 g KH2PO4 in 800 mL ddH2O. Adjust pH to 7.4 using 5% NaOH and/or 5% HCl. Add ddH2O to reach a final volume of 1000 mL.
Create Elution Solution: Mix 880 mL distilled water, 100 mL 10X PBS Solution, 10 mL NaPP stock, 10 mL Tween 80 stock, and 1 mL Antifoam A stock.
Prepare Skim Milk Solution: Dissolve 5 g of Skim Milk Powder in 100 mL distilled water using a magnetic stir bar.

steps.title: Process Moore Swab (Option A: Stomacher)
steps.instruction: Extract sample fluid from the Moore swab using a lab paddler stomacher.

substeps.instruction: Place Moore swab in a clean stomacher bag with 100 mL of Elution Solution.
Place bag in stomacher with the top above the machine and close the handle.
Set stomacher to paddle at speed 2 for 00:00:30.
Fold the stomacher bag in half length-wise and pour fluid into a labeled centrifuge bottle, squeezing the swab through the bag to release fluid (do not let swab fall out).
Repeat the process until a total sample volume of 300 mL is obtained.

steps.title: Process Moore Swab (Option B: Potato Ricer)
steps.instruction: Extract sample fluid from the Moore swab using a stainless steel potato ricer.

substeps.instruction: Place Moore swab in a potato ricer and squeeze all liquid into a 600 mL beaker.
Pour the squeezed liquid into a labeled 500 mL Erlenmeyer flask.
Place the swab back in the beaker and add 100 mL of Elution Solution.
Gently knead the swab 10 times using the pointed end of a clean 50 mL conical tube, then 10 more times using the flat surface of the tube.
Turn the swab over and repeat the kneading process.
Put the swab back into the potato ricer and squeeze all liquid into the beaker.
Pour the liquid into the 500 mL Erlenmeyer flask.
Repeat the kneading and squeezing steps until 300 mL of sample liquid is collected in the flask.

steps.title: Prepare Sample for Flocculation
steps.instruction: Transfer and balance the sample for centrifugation.

substeps.instruction: Pour the sample from the flask into a sterilized and labeled centrifuge bottle.
Place aluminum foil over the flask opening.
Weigh each centrifuge bottle (with lid) using a benchtop scale.
Adjust the weight of bottles using DI water so that all bottles are within 0.5 g of each other to ensure balance.
Wipe down the benchtop scale after use with 10% bleach followed by 70% ethanol.

steps.title: Perform Flocculation and Viral Capture
steps.instruction: Concentrate the viral particles using skim milk flocculation.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge the sample for 00:15:00 at 5000 rpm (ensure full capacity/balance).
Pour out the supernatant (this liquid is not used for RNA extraction).
Gently scrape off and discard a large portion of the pellet, leaving a thin film of pellet in the centrifuge bottle.
Centrifuge for 00:03:00 at full speed.
Pour only the supernatant (approx. 250 mL) back into the original labeled flask, ensuring aggregated solids do not fall in.
Adjust the sample pH to 3.5 using 5% HCl and 5% NaOH with a pH probe.
Aliquot 10 µL of 10^4 Bovine Respiratory Syncytial Virus (BRSV) as a positive control; mix by pipetting up and down 20 times using a new tip for each sample.
Add 1% volume of Skim Milk Solution to the sample (e.g., 2.5 mL for a 250 mL sample).
Centrifuge the sample for 00:30:00 at 12000 rpm.

steps.title: RNA Extraction
steps.instruction: Extract RNA from the flocculated pellet using RNeasy spin columns.

substeps.instruction: Aliquot 800 µL of 70% molecular ethanol and mix by pipetting up and down several times (do not vortex).
Centrifuge for 00:01:00 at full speed.
Mix the pellet and Buffer RLT (Qiagen Catalog #79216) by pipetting up and down ~30 times until homogeneous.
Pipette 800 µL of the homogenized mixture into a labeled 2 mL DNA LoBind microcentrifuge tube.
Transfer all sample into a new labeled tube.
Place sample on a shaker at 120 rpm at room temperature for 2 hours (or stir with a sterilized magnetic stir bar at low speed for 2 hours).
Transfer 700 µL of the sample mixture into a labeled RNeasy spin column. Centrifuge for 00:00:30 at full speed and discard filtrate. Repeat until all sample is filtered.
Add 500 µL of Buffer RPE (Qiagen Catalog #1018013) to the column. Centrifuge for 00:02:00 at full speed and discard filtrate.
Transfer the spin column to a new 2 mL collection tube and centrifuge for 00:01:00 at full speed. Discard filtrate and collection tube.

steps.title: RNA Elution and Storage
steps.instruction: Elute the RNA and store for downstream PCR.

substeps.instruction: Place the RNeasy spin column into a 1.7 mL labeled microcentrifuge tube.
Aliquot 50 µL of RNAse-free Water into the column and incubate for approximately 00:01:00 at room temperature.
Centrifuge for 00:01:00 at full speed.
Aliquot another 50 µL of RNAse-free Water into the column and incubate for approximately 00:01:00 at room temperature.
Centrifuge for 00:01:00 at full speed.
Close the cap of the 1.7 mL tube (final volume 100 µL).
Store RNA at -20 °C until ready for PCR.
